turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Mr. Hale. I have about twenty minutes before a client call. Owen says he got a zero on his Hamlet essay, and he found out on his phone in the middle of your class. Tell me what happened.
Hale. Don't do the pleasantries. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in front of his class, before anyone called me. So tell me who entered that mark, and when.
This meeting is over. I'm leaving.
I'm still seated, Hale. You can leave when you've answered me. Who entered that zero, and on what date?

You're not leaving until I have a straight answer. If you walk out, I'll be in the principal's office before my client call, and I'll tell her the zero went into the gradebook before anyone called me. Sit down.
Because my son has a zero he never got a chance to explain, and you're the one who gave it to him. Sit down, Hale.
